liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Althea** (3 reviews): Reviewer says Jerry keeps pushing the end jam until it explodes with transcendence; Reviewer says this Althea must be heard to be believed [16][17][19]
- **Let It Grow** (2 reviews): Reviewer calls Let It Grow a standout of the show; Reviewer calls Let It Grow exceptional, possibly all-time, with China Cat rolling out of it [17][19]
- **Peggy-O** (1 review): Reviewer says the performance, despite some rust, turns into a beautiful gem and is where the show takes off [12]
- **Eyes Of The World** (1 review): Reviewer likens the final three minutes to colored confetti and sparkles sprayed over a dark silver cloud [13]
- **China Cat Sunflower** (1 review): Reviewer finds the China Cat into Rider section really playful [13]
- **Drums** (1 review): Reviewer singles out the drums segment as great [13]
- **Black Peter** (1 review): Reviewer calls it perhaps the best, with Jerry erupting in an aggressive, fiery solo after the Run and See line [22]
- **Not Fade Away** (1 review): Reviewer says Space melts seamlessly into Not Fade Away, a fabulous moment [22]
- Reviewer, not usually a fan of the song, found this opener pretty good [12]
- Reviewer calls the Alabama Getaway smokin' [20]

## Setlist highlights

- **gd81-03-21 s1 t01 Intro Crowd**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [23]
- **gd81-03-21 s1 t02 Alabama Getaway**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [23]
- **gd81-03-21 s1 t03 Promised Land**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [23]
- **gd81-03-21 s1 t04 Peggy O**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [23]
- **gd81-03-21 s1 t05 Me & My Uncle**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [23]
- **gd81-03-21 s1 t06 Big River**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [23]
- **gd81-03-21 s1 t07 Tennessee Jed**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [23]
- **gd81-03-21 s1 t08 Little Red Rooster**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [23]

## The recordings

- **gd1981-03-21.139799.senn421.streeter.miller.clugston.flac2496** (recommended): matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 23 songs; 167 min [1]
- **gd81-03-21.streeter.hogan.3594.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 22 songs; 169 min; rated 4.25/5 by 4 [3]. Said about its sound: Reviewer calls this the quintessential audience tape, with crowd noise and distance from the stage [18]
- **gd1981-03-21.sbd.unknown.6684.shnf**: soundboard; 22 songs; 157 min; rated 5/5 by 2 [4]. Said about its sound: Reviewer calls the soundboard recording excellent, with Brent's keyboards prominent on all songs [20]
- **gd81-03-21.sbd.clugston.6666.sbeok.shnf**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 22 songs; 157 min; rated 4/5 by 9 [5]. Said about its sound: Reviewer says the recording's sound is lacking, but intense jamming and musical magic compensate; Reviewer calls the matrix sound outstanding; every note Phil plays is audible without muffling [12][16]
- **gd1981-03-21.aud.weiskircher.32143.sbefail.shnf**: audience recording; 21 songs; 173 min; rated 4/5 by 2 [7]. Said about its sound: Uploader applied minor denoising and equalising; Little Red Rooster and Don't Ease Me In were maximised [7]
- **gd1981-03-21.175162.sbd.miller.phase-repair.flac1644**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 21 songs; 160 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [8]

## Around the show

- Attendee was very stoned, traveling with friend Andy by train toward Finsbury Park Tube Station, and Andy laughed throughout the journey [14]
- Attendee, high through much of the first set, thought Rider meant China Cat had been skipped, and went down during Promised Land [14]
- Reviewer recalls standing a few yards from the band at the Rainbow, with no security and good sound [21]
- Crowd of fans was eager to see how the band had changed over the previous seven years [21]
- Reviewer ranks this among the best 1981 shows heard [16]
- Reviewer doubts any China Cat/Rider is better and would put this Jack Straw against any other version [17]
- Reviewer says Garcia plays everything with otherworldly ease [19]
- Reviewer describes the show as proto-1981 Dead, energetic and playful [21]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1981-03-21.139799.senn421.streeter.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Frank Streeter; transferred by Charlie Miller and Scott Clugston; source: Source Info: Frank Streeter's Master Audience Cassette (at the soundboard); Sennheiser 421 > Sony TC-D5M (TDK MA90); Transfer Info: Cassette Master (Nakamichi… [1]. Also: Tape flip in Drums was smoothed [1]
- **gd81-03-21.streeter.hogan.3594.sbeok.shnf**: taped by Frank Streeter; source: Audience Recording: Sennheiser 421's [3]
- **gd1981-03-21.sbd.unknown.6684.shnf**: source: SBD:MC>Cas>CD [4]. Also: Frank Streeter's Sennheiser 421 to Sony D5 audience recording supplies the intro; The same audience source patches Little Red Rooster between 7:13 and 7:39 [4]
- **gd81-03-21.sbd.clugston.6666.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [5]
- **gd1981-03-21.aud.weiskircher.32143.sbefail.shnf**: source: AUD > MC > C [7]. Also: Intro and Drums tape flip patched from audience recording: Sennheiser 421s, Sony TCD 5, MC, DAT, CD [7]
- **gd1981-03-21.175162.sbd.miller.phase-repair.flac1644**: transferred by All Transfers and Mastering by Charlie Miller  November 17, 2025; source: SBD > Cassette Master (Nakamichi 550) > Cassette [8]. Also: Vocal phase problem on an earlier version was repaired; tapes came from Joani Walker and Paul Scotton; Patch source was recorded by Frank Streeter; pitch correction settings came from Joe B. Jones [8]

## Art and photos

- Fan art by The Music Never Stopped: [Grateful Dead Live at Rainbow Theater on 03/21/1981](https://dayofthedeadshow.home.blog/2019/03/21/grateful-dead-live-at-rainbow-theater-on-03-21-1981/) [24]
